name: Shema
overview: Shema was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Elpaal. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes provided beyond his genealogical placement. This establishes him as part of the Benjaminite lineage recorded in 1 Chronicles 8.
namesAndTitles: The name Shema means 'he hears,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with significance related to hearing or listening. Another related name, Shimei, meaning 'YHWH has heard' or 'famous,' appears in the same chapter but refers to a different individual. These names highlight a common theme of divine attentiveness in the Benjaminite genealogy.
familyAndRelationships: Shema is explicitly identified as the son of Elpaal. Inferred paternal relationships in the same genealogical context include Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath, though these are not directly linked to Shema himself. Beyond his father Elpaal, Scripture does not record further family relationships for Shema.
scriptureSignificance: Shema's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, as preserved in 1 Chronicles 8. This genealogy traces the lineage of Benjaminite families, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people. While Shema himself is not associated with specific events or roles, his mention contributes to the biblical record of Israel's tribal heritage.
